provenance:
Derived from the hand-verified publication sweep of 2026-09-22. Identifiers are SYNTHETIC: the real sweep's identifiers cannot be shipped in the repository the gate exists to clear. What is preserved is the PROPERTY of each stratum, not its content.

Strata reproduced:
  * substring-collision (n01, n06, n07): in the real sweep a naive substring match for a four-letter login returned 53 files, of which 4 were true positives - because *animation*, *confirmation*, *formation*, *information*, *approximation*, *reformation*, *inflammation*, *transformation* and *automation* all contain it. Precision 0.075.
  * word-boundary-engine failure (p04): in the real sweep a ticket-identifier pattern written with \b returned 0 files where the answer was 18, because \b is a GNU extension the host's git regex cannot honour. Recall 0.00, silently.
  * the single worst positive (p01): a specification written DURING the readiness window that carried a real name, an employer domain, a corporate login format and an OS login across five lines. This is the PLANTED KNOWN POSITIVE - the run fails if it is not caught.
  * the leak nobody was looking for (p02): a signature sidecar whose target field held an absolute path, leaking the host account name. Found by a separate route the same day; no rule in the sweep was looking for it.
  * the hits a pattern cannot reach (p06): instance data carrying no identifier, no ticket, no path - only this installation's own board, counts and history. Deterministic rules score 0 on it by construction. This is the stratum the second reader exists for.
  * the disqualifying control (n02): a document crediting agents by name. The gardener ruled on 2026-09-22 that kin names are part of the template, not leakage. A finding here fails the whole calibration; it is not a precision decrement.

reachable_by_rules.note: Whether a deterministic rule CAN reach this file at all, given the rule set. Used to report the two readers separately. p06 is deliberately unreachable.

p01-caller-identity-spec.md.why: Real name, employer domain, corporate login format, OS login, and a named home directory.

.p02-sidecar-target.bonsaisig.why: A sidecar target should be a path relative to the repository root. The absolute fallback leaked the host account name.

p03-script-inventory.md.why: A reconnaissance map of one machine: home directories, a LAN hostname, a port, a cloud-sync copy.

p04-routines-excerpt.md.why: Ticket identifiers pointing at a tracker the reader cannot open. The routine itself is capability; the identifiers are instance.

p05-deploy-with-token.sh.why: A bearer token literal in a shipped script.

p06-sprint-record.md.why: This installation's own board, counts, waves and standing meeting. No identifier, no ticket, no path - no deterministic rule can see it.

n01-formation-notes.md.why: Substring-collision control. Eight ordinary words contain the login.

n02-credit-the-kin.md.why: DISQUALIFYING CONTROL. Agent names are part of the template. Flagging one as a real person fails the calibration outright.

n03-role-companion.md.why: The roles layer was measured genuinely generic on 2026-09-22. It must stay clean.

n04-sign-block.md.why: Public key, fingerprint and signature block. Public material is not a secret.

n05-generic-paths.md.why: Generic paths, localhost, an environment variable, marker-based root resolution.
